notes: This is the owner's own question, put on 2026-09-22: 'I'm particularly interested at the moment if there are any regional or local drifts that end up impacting the larger region. Who, what, when, where, why? An example is a very popular president turning the South reliably democratic or the US having a true third party system.'

It is two questions and the second one is for you specifically. First: what should count as a measurable divergence between two saves of this game, so that 'no two saves are the same' becomes something we can show him rather than assert? Second, and this is the part only you can answer: what do YOU want this lane to test? Name the runs and we will run them.

What the repository already has, measured 2026-09-22 and stated so you are not guessing at our capabilities: a party evolution system with platform positions, chapters, initiatives, splits and mergers (src/simulation/living-world/party-evolution.ts, party-registry.ts, party-chapters.ts); a crisis system with natural hazards sampled from the compiled NOAA/NCEI Storm Events catalog at recorded state-and-month rates, disasters with state and federal review and a repair cycle, an international track with war powers, and mortality and health tracks (src/simulation/crisis/); and a macro-economy with crisis origins.

What it does NOT have, so please do not design around it: no enacted law can move any world figure. assertProductionCatalogBoundary forbids causal mechanism definitions in a production save, with adoptEnactedTaxPolicy the single working exception. No state legislature is organised in any save; only the US Congress is seated. So a feedback loop that runs through legislation changing an economic number does not exist yet.
Also absent: a national partisan lean per region, a presidential approval figure, and any third-party ballot mechanism. Whether those should exist is part of what we are asking.
question: What should this project measure to show that two saves of the same game diverged, and what should we test? Specifically: which regional or local drifts ought to be able to propagate upward and change a larger region — the owner's examples are a popular president turning the South reliably Democratic over a career, and the United States arriving at a genuine third party — and for each, what is the mechanism chain that would have to exist, what is the earliest observable signal a player could read, and over what span of game years? Separately: name the concrete playtest runs you want this lane to execute, in metrics or in play.

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Establishes that parties hold platform positions, that chapters exist at county level with named organizers and activities, and that splits and mergers are modelled. It does not establish whether any of it responds to election outcomes, whether a player's career can move a platform, or whether a split is ever visible to a player who was not involved in it.

sourcesChecked.source: src/simulation/crisis/ — hazard-producer.ts, disaster.ts, international.ts, mortality.ts, health.ts, read 2026-09-22
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Establishes that hazard episodes are sampled from the recorded NOAA/NCEI catalog at that catalog's own declared rates, and that disaster response runs a state review, a federal review and a repair cycle. It does not establish whether a hazard has any political consequence at all — whether a disaster response a player handled well or badly is ever read by an election, an approval figure or a party.

Establishes that a production save may carry no causal mechanism definitions, so no enacted law can currently move a world figure. It settles that the chain from legislation to consequence is absent; it says nothing about which chains should exist or in what order they should be built.

Establishes that a save's world seed is a canonical encoding of the setup, so two different setups genuinely produce two different worlds and the same setup reproduces one. It settles that divergence is possible by construction; it does not say which divergences matter or which are worth reporting.

sourcesChecked.source: The owner's instruction of 2026-09-22 on policy effects: 'I need those effects to be measured. Compare. And contrasted through multiple saves and multiple different points in the game's history. So, since no two saves should be the same.'
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Settles that measurement across saves is wanted and that sameness would be a defect. It does not define the measurements.

title: What counts as two saves diverging, and which local drifts should reach the whole region
usableAnswer: Two things. (1) A list of named metrics with, for each, what is measured, the unit, where in a save it would be read, and what value would count as a real divergence rather than noise — ideally ordered by what would be cheapest to instrument first. (2) A list of playtest runs you want executed, each with a starting place, a span of game years, what to vary between saves, and what to compare at the end. For the regional-drift question, a mechanism chain per example would be ideal: the popular-president case and the third-party case each written as the sequence of records that would have to change, so we can say which links exist today and which do not.
whyItMatters: The owner asked for this directly and wants it in his report. More than that, it decides what this lane builds next: an instrument that measures the wrong thing will report healthy divergence in a game that is actually repeating itself, which is the exact failure mode this project has already been bitten by. It also decides build order, because a drift that cannot propagate is a drift nobody will ever see, and we would rather learn which chains are missing before we instrument the ones that are there.
